    Track 4 · Advanced · Lesson 3

    Knowledge distillation II: the KD loss

    After this lesson you can read and reason about the KD loss alpha·CE + (1−alpha)·T²·KL — what temperature does, why the T² factor is there, and how alpha trades off the gold label against the teacher.

    Level: advanced Read time: ~11 min Prerequisites: Knowledge distillation I: the teacher and capturing its logits Updated: 13 Nov 2026

    You have the teacher's soft targets saved. The student learns from them through a loss with two parts: the ordinary supervised loss against the gold label, and a divergence from the teacher's distribution. BrewSLM's offline KD loss is:

    loss = alpha * CE(student, gold_label)  +  (1 - alpha) * T^2 * KL(teacher_T || student_T)

    Term one: cross-entropy on the hard label

    This is the SFT loss you already know (Track 1's cross-entropy lesson): the student is penalized for not putting probability on the correct gold token. It keeps the student anchored to the truth, even if the teacher is occasionally wrong.

    Term two: KL divergence to the teacher

    KL divergence measures how far the student's distribution is from the teacher's. Minimizing it pulls the student's whole output distribution toward the teacher's — transferring the dark knowledge. We compute it on temperature-softened distributions.

    The direction matters, because KL is not symmetric. KL(teacher ‖ student) is the forward KL of Hinton et al. (2015): it averages over the teacher's distribution, so the student is penalized for missing any token the teacher gives weight to (mode-covering). The reverse KL, KL(student ‖ teacher), is mode-seeking — the student may concentrate on the teacher's main mode — and is the choice some newer methods for generative students make (MiniLLM, Gu et al., 2024).

    Temperature: softening the distribution

    Dividing logits by a temperature T before softmax flattens the distribution. At T=1 you get the normal probabilities; at T=2–4 the differences shrink, so small probabilities on the runner-up tokens become visible — and those secondary probabilities are precisely the relational signal you want to transfer. A peaky 99/1 distribution teaches almost nothing about the runner-up; at T=2 it becomes about 91/9, and at T≈3.3 about 80/20.

    Why the T² factor?

    Softening by T shrinks the gradients of the KL term by roughly 1/T². Multiplying the KL term by T² rescales them back, so the soft-target loss keeps a consistent magnitude as you change temperature — and stays balanced against the CE term.

    Alpha: how much teacher vs how much truth

    alpha in [0,1] balances the two terms. alpha → 1 leans on the gold labels (closer to plain SFT); alpha → 0 leans on the teacher's soft targets. A middle value is a common start: learn from the teacher's nuance while staying pinned to the ground truth. BrewSLM's offline KD recipes (recipe.kd.*) default to alpha=0.5, T=2.0. Tune the two together on a dev split, not on the gold set you report.

    On the platform

    A BrewSLM run reaches offline KD two ways: in the Train form, More options → Training presets → apply an Offline KD preset (recipe.kd.*; it sets training_mode: distillation, distillation_offline: true, alpha and temperature), or through the experiment API: POST /api/projects/{id}/training/experiments accepts training_mode: distillation (or distillation_offline: true) plus distillation_capture_path and distillation_offline_top_k (defaults distillation/teacher_capture.jsonl and 8). The capture file must sit inside the project's own data folder (by default its distillation/teacher_capture.jsonl), distillation_offline_top_k is at most 20, and offline KD together with live-teacher KD (distillation_enabled) is refused. The Training Mode list itself offers only SFT, continued pretraining, DPO and ORPO, so after applying an Offline KD preset it can't display the mode it will send (Lesson 3.11).

    That balance only holds if both terms are measured per scored token. Mask the prompt and padding out of both terms; if the KL term sums over every position while the CE term averages over answer tokens, the KL term is many times larger and alpha=0.5 no longer means half and half.

    In code

    import torch.nn.functional as F

def kd_loss(student_logits, teacher_logits, labels, alpha=0.5, T=2.0):
    # causal LM: the logits at position t predict token t+1, so shift by one
    s = student_logits[:, :-1, :].reshape(-1, student_logits.size(-1))
    t = teacher_logits[:, :-1, :].reshape(-1, teacher_logits.size(-1))
    y = labels[:, 1:].reshape(-1)

    # keep only scored positions (prompt and padding are -100) for BOTH terms
    keep = y != -100
    s, t, y = s[keep], t[keep], y[keep]

    # term 1: hard-label cross-entropy (the SFT loss), mean per token
    ce = F.cross_entropy(s, y)

    # term 2: KL(teacher_T || student_T). kl_div takes the student's log-probs
    # first and the teacher's probs second; "batchmean" over [N, V] rows = per token
    s_log = F.log_softmax(s / T, dim=-1)
    t_prob = F.softmax(t / T, dim=-1)
    kl = F.kl_div(s_log, t_prob, reduction="batchmean") * (T * T)

    return alpha * ce + (1.0 - alpha) * kl

    This mirrors BrewSLM's loss: a pure kd_loss function over the flattened, masked positions, used by the offline kd_trainer, selected by setting training_mode="distillation" and a recipe.kd.* recipe. The trainer reads teacher_capture.jsonl (the top-k logprobs from Lesson 4.2) and fills the tokens outside the top-k with a large negative logit to build the teacher term. Otherwise it's the same training loop you already know — only the loss changed. The last distillation lesson asks the real question: how much of the teacher's quality did the student actually keep?

    Key idea

    The KD loss is alpha·CE + (1−alpha)·T²·KL(teacher ‖ student), both terms over the same scored tokens: cross-entropy anchors the student to the gold label; temperature-softened KL transfers the teacher's distribution; T² keeps the soft term's magnitude stable; alpha dials teacher-vs-truth. Same loop, richer loss.

    Key terms

    KD loss
    alpha·CE + (1−alpha)·T²·KL — the blend of hard-label cross-entropy and teacher KL.
    KL divergence
    A measure of how far the student's distribution is from the teacher's; minimized to transfer knowledge. KD classically uses the forward direction, KL(teacher ‖ student).
    temperature (T)
    A divisor on logits before softmax; higher T softens the distribution to expose secondary probabilities.
    T² factor
    Rescales the KL term to offset the 1/T² gradient shrink from softening, keeping the term balanced.
    alpha
    The [0,1] weight trading the gold-label CE term against the teacher KL term.
    kd_trainer
    BrewSLM's offline distillation trainer that applies kd_loss against the captured teacher logprobs.
